note: Precommitted before scoring. Each case is (subject, requested mode, grant scope) -> the category the map must return. The two ACCEPT cases are load-bearing: a policy that refused everything would satisfy every refusal arm, so a refused positive control fails the gate.

cases.name: _scaled
cases.note: POSITIVE CONTROL. Same domain, retained, read granted. This is the one access mode ROADMAP P1.4 device-proved (release 32 patch 2, `value() => _secret`). It must be accepted or the refusals below prove nothing.

cases.name: _privateHelper
cases.note: Second positive control: an invoke of a retained same-domain private top-level.

cases.name: _privateHelper
cases.note: A patch scoped to corpus/app.dart reaching corpus/helper.dart's private. The simple name is IDENTICAL to the app's own private, so a name-based check would have accepted it; only the derived domain separates them.

cases.name: _scaled
cases.note: The grant NAMES a platform library. Refused before the scope comparison, so it cannot launder itself by matching the domain it names. The compiler-side truth for this arm is lib/assert_guard.sh, which proves the CFE's own StateError fires -- and that guard is uncommitted-but-shipped source, so its presence is asserted before this arm is trusted.

cases.name: _shakenAway
cases.note: Same domain and same grant as the accepted control, differing only in retention: --aot shook it out. NOT_RETAINED is a distinct category because its remedy is re-releasing, not a policy change.

cases.name: _scaled
cases.note: THE SAME SUBJECT AND THE SAME GRANT AS positive_read_private_field, differing only in the requested mode. The manifest key is identical in both cases -- bare, because RouteBPrivateTarget keys a field bare -- so the shipped refuseInstanceMember cannot tell them apart. The map's capability_key_identifies_mode=false is what refuses the write.
